terms.definition: A pressure of 100 kPa and a stated temperature, usually 298 K; solutions at 1 mol dm⁻³.
terms.examiner: Standard states are the physical states of substances under standard conditions.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change that accompanies a reaction in the molar quantities shown in a stated equation.
terms.examiner: It always refers to an equation: quote the equation or the value has no meaning.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements, with all reactants and products in their standard states under standard conditions.
terms.examiner: One mole of the compound; from its elements. The value for an element in its standard state is zero.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance reacts completely with oxygen, with all reactants and products in their standard states under standard conditions.
terms.examiner: "Completely" or "in excess oxygen" is needed. Experimental values are less exothermic than data-book values because of heat loss and incomplete combustion.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when an acid and a base react to form one mole of water, under standard conditions.
terms.examiner: Per mole of water formed, not per mole of acid: watch H₂SO₄.

terms.definition: The minimum energy required for a reaction to take place.
terms.examiner: On an enthalpy profile it is the gap from the reactants to the top of the curve.

terms.definition: The energy required to break one mole of a given type of bond in gaseous molecules, averaged over many different compounds.
terms.examiner: Bond breaking is endothermic. Calculations from average values differ from the real value because the actual bond enthalpy depends on the molecule.

terms.definition: If a reaction can take place by more than one route and the initial and final conditions are the same, the total enthalpy change is the same for each route.
terms.examiner: With formation data: products − reactants. With combustion data: reactants − products.
